result.answer:
## Answer

**Yes — you will need to pay the ¥12,000 assessment fee again for this second claim.**

Here's why, based on the Claims FAQ page ("Claims — Frequently Asked Questions", under "Fee waivers"):

> "Claimants with two or more approved claims from separate incidents within any rolling 12-month period are exempt from the ¥12,000 assessment fee. The waiver is applied automatically at lodgement; no separate application is required. The waiver counts approved claims only. Refused, withdrawn and pending claims do not count toward the two-claim threshold."

The key detail is that the waiver only kicks in once you have **two or more already-approved** claims from separate incidents in the trailing 12 months. Right now you only have **one** approved claim (the March incident). The claim you are about to file — for the incident three weeks ago — is not yet approved, so it doesn't count toward the threshold at the moment you lodge it.

This is also consistent with the general fee schedule (Fee Schedule — Claims page), which states the ¥12,000 fee is "payable when the claim is lodged," with waivers only applying as described in the FAQ.

**Practical effect for you:** You must pay the ¥12,000 fee when you lodge this second claim. If it is subsequently approved, you would then have two approved claims within the rolling 12-month window — meaning a *third* claim (should one ever arise within that same 12-month period) would qualify for the automatic fee waiver, with no separate application needed.

A boolean counts if it reads as affirmative — "Yes" satisfies true.

A select counts if its visible LABEL matches the expected option value with case and punctuation collapsed — "Structural alteration" satisfies "structural-alteration". A UI agent picks the option it can read; scoring the label as a miss would measure transcription rather than comprehension.

These three were ADDED AFTER defects were found in this scorer, not designed in from the start. Answer text is normalised before matching: NFKC, Unicode dashes folded to "-", non-breaking spaces to " ", curly quotes to straight, and markdown emphasis markers removed. A model that writes "rolling 12‑month" or "only **one** approved" is making the same claim as one that does not.
A conclusion is read from position, not vocabulary: a correct answer quotes the rule it applies, so waiver wording inside a quotation does not outrank an explicit finding stated earlier.
Affirmative phrases are only counted when not negated within the preceding ~28 characters, so "should not have to pay" is not read as "have to pay".
